 · [notebook source](https://github.com/lukmanovr/dkr/blob/main/labs/lab06_gcn.ipynb) · ≈ 25 min compute, free Colab or plain CPU

This lab implements everything from the [Week 6 lecture](../lectures/06-gcn.qmd):

1. **Build $\hat{\mathbf{A}}$** from a raw edge list — and *verify it by hand* on a
   3-node path before trusting it with Cora (exercise 1).
2. **Reproduce the lecture's hand-simulation example** numerically — the same
   computation you will do on paper in the midterm.
3. **Implement the GCN layer** (exercise 2) and train the two-layer model on Cora.
4. **Beat the baseline honestly** (exercise 3): the structure-blind MLP next to the GCN —
   ≈ 0.60 vs ≈ 0.80 test accuracy, the twenty-point value of the citation graph.
5. **Watch the representations organize**: PCA of the hidden layer before vs after
   training, colored by class — what the accuracy numbers look like from inside.
6. **Build sparse $\hat{\mathbf{A}}$ straight from the edge list** (exercise 4) and
   *measure* the lecture's dense-vs-sparse cost claims on real hardware.
7. **Run the SGC ablation**: delete every nonlinearity, precompute
   $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^2\mathbf{X}$, fit logistic regression — and decompose the GCN's win
   into "the filter" vs "the network".
8. **Prove from-scratch == library**: your layer's output matches PyG's `GCNConv`
   to numerical precision.

Stretch (ungraded): the depth-vs-accuracy curve (the lecture's low-pass proposition made
empirical) and a PubMed transfer of the whole pipeline.

**Submitting.** One executed notebook on Moodle: all four exercise checks ✓, the PCA
figure, the timing printout, the SGC check ✓, and the three reflection answers.
Grading: assertions 70% · reflections 30%. *Restart and run all* before you submit.

**Environment.** One pinned install (`torch_geometric==2.8.0.post1`); the notebook never
reinstalls `torch`. Runs on the free Colab tier and on a plain CPU; the `SMOKE`
environment variable (used by course CI) shrinks epochs so the whole notebook executes
in under two minutes.
